chapter: New York, Henderson and Charlie Johnson
title: Doc Hyder's band personnel and the sax player who never bought a reed
summary: A 12-13 piece band including Bernard Archer, Lincoln Mills, Wilkins, Puny and Watkins, a brilliant reed player who never bought a reed.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well Herman, we were talking before, you were in Philadelphia playing with Doc Hyder band.
How big a band was that?

Aw, he had what, 12 or 13 pieces then, had a big band, you know. Well I always thought we had three or four brass, and same with saxes, and you know, and the rhythm, and whatnot. And had some good musicians, too.

Well, Bernard ARcher, trombone player. I happen to remember right off. Lincoln Mills, trumpet player. He's gone now. Elmoore, Elmer, Elber, Wilkins, drummer. Used to call him Shorty. I'm trying to think of some of the saxophone players now. Puny -- Puny, what's your right name? He played the baritone sax, and very, very good. I'm trying to think -- oh, here's a guy, Watkins. He played clarinet, alto saxophone, one of the finest musicians that I've ever met in my life. He was in the band.

This guy -- why I'm mentioning him, besides being such a terrific musician, never bought a reed in his life.

(Laughter.)

Now that sounds -- may sound funny.
How did he play the saxophone, never

bought a reed? Okay. Other guys would buy a reed, and say aw, this isn't my type, it doesn't lay on -- you know, you've seen some saxophone players take a reed, they turn it upside down, they turn it -- (laughs) you know, and get tight, get mad, and temperamental, I say. Throw them away. He would pick itup and take it and put it on his saxophone, and sound beautiful.

And he would keep it there for years until it would -- oh man, it would rot. It would turn black. It would turn water-soaked, everything. And he never worried. And you never heard anyone with a tone as good, or better, than his. I have never.
His technique, terrific. He sounds -- when he played the clarinet it sounded like the wind was blowing, ffhvoo, ffhvoo, you know? The guy was something.

Andy Gumps -- that was his nickname. We used to call him. Oh, he was a heck of a guy. And he was in the band. Who else? Can I think? Well, that's all the saxophone players that I can name right off, right off.
